title: Constitutional Acts and Reforms in British India: Quiz

questions.question: The post of Governor-General of Bengal was created by:
questions.rationale: The 1773 Act made Warren Hastings Governor-General of Bengal. The 1833 Act later created the Governor-General of India.

questions.question: Which Act set up the Board of Control and the system of dual control?
questions.rationale: The Board of Control handled political matters and the Court of Directors commercial ones. The Regulating Act of 1773 came earlier.

questions.question: Which Charter Act ended the East India Company's trade monopoly in India (tea and China trade excepted)?
questions.rationale: The Act of 1813 ended the monopoly in India. The 1833 Act ended the Company's remaining commercial functions.

questions.question: The Charter Act of 1833 is known for:
options: Creating the Governor-General of India, with Bentinck as the first
Starting open competition for the civil service
questions.rationale: Bentinck was first Governor-General of India. Open competition came in 1853 and Company rule ended in 1858.

questions.question: Open competition for recruitment to the civil service was introduced by the:
questions.rationale: The 1853 Act, the last Charter Act, opened the service to competition, followed by the Macaulay Committee of 1854.

questions.question: Which Act ended the rule of the East India Company and created the Secretary of State for India?
options: Act for the Better Government of India, 1858
questions.rationale: After the Revolt of 1857, the Act of 1858 transferred power to the Crown and set up the Secretary of State with a Council of India.

questions.question: The portfolio system was introduced by which Act?
questions.rationale: The 1861 Act, under Canning, divided the Viceroy's council into departments. The 1892 Act brought indirect election and budget discussion.

questions.question: Which Act provided separate electorates for Muslims?
questions.rationale: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 gave Muslims separate electorates. The 1919 Act extended the principle to Sikhs and others.

questions.question: Dyarchy at the provincial level was introduced by the:
questions.rationale: Dyarchy split provincial subjects into reserved and transferred ones in 1919. The 1935 Act replaced it with provincial autonomy.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?
options: Reserved and transferred subjects in provinces
Office of High Commissioner for India in London
questions.rationale: The Federal Court came with the 1935 Act (in 1937). The other three were 1919 features.

questions.question: Provincial autonomy was introduced in 1937 under the:
questions.rationale: The 1935 Act replaced provincial dyarchy with autonomy, and provincial elections were held for the new arrangement in 1937.

questions.question: Which body or institution was established under the Government of India Act, 1935 provisions?
options: Federal Court and the Reserve Bank of India
Council of State and Legislative Assembly
questions.rationale: The Federal Court (1937) and RBI link to the 1935 Act. The Council of State came in 1919, the Board of Control in 1784, and the Calcutta court in 1773.

questions.question: The Montagu Declaration of August 1917 promised:
options: Gradual development of self-governing institutions and responsible government
questions.rationale: Montagu's statement of 1917 set the stage for the 1919 Act. Dominion status was not promised, and partition came in 1947.

questions.question: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 received royal assent on:
questions.rationale: The Act received assent on 18 July and took effect on 15 August 1947, creating the two dominions.

questions.question: The Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) and the council of four for the Governor-General were provisions of the:
questions.rationale: Both were created under the 1773 Act. Pitt's Act set up the Board of Control instead.
